why: A point with one subject and one resolving root is all ROOT_POINT asks. It has no extent and does not pretend to.
Work with no product ground behind it can only be prioritised on opinion.
A root recorded and unresolvable is worse than no root: it reads as traced.
The path traverses contract, service and conformance, and ends on a check somebody else can re-run.
GROUND-010. A path ending on a report has the participant that produced it as its only evidence, and every later stage inherits that.
Two closed verticals, a shared boundary, and an estimate on the dimension the stage requires.
Composition multiplies the gap, and the join hides which half failed.
HORIZONTAL_SURFACE is the stage at which the work can honestly be sized. Advancing without sizing it skips the only thing the stage adds.
Every operation declares its six parts, and what discovery advertises is what the endpoint checks.
The live instance is nine BUILT console operations declaring an authority and checking none, console.grant among them. The surface looked complete from either side alone.
The other half of the same defect. An endpoint reachable and absent from discovery cannot be found by a participant arriving with no briefing, and is reachable anyway by one that guesses.
Admitted identity, a typed check and a receipt on every operation, and an observation from a participant with no build relation.
A node that witnesses itself closed its circuit with itself at both ends.
Operating successfully is not identity. This is the gap STATUS.yaml records as NO_ADMISSION_TRANSITION.
Each stage admission predicate is the previous stage evidence, so a surface claimed straight from a point is a claim about nothing.
A stage name the circuit does not declare is reported, never treated as the nearest thing.
A range on every required dimension, from a named estimator.
A dimension the registry does not declare is reported rather than dropped, so it cannot appear on one side of a boundary only.
A low above its high is not a wide estimate, it is a typo that orders a board wrongly.
A single number hides whether the estimator knew the shape of the work. The width of the range is the more useful reading.
A ticket at or past a dimension's required stage owes an estimate on it.
The estimator may record what it measured and may not settle what the gap means. That is an observation, and an observation from inside the build is not one.
Nothing measures a story point after the fact. An actual on one would be the estimate compared to itself.
One resolving root, a runnable closure check, a settling seat that is not the holder, and an estimate on what ROOT_POINT requires.
